entries.plain: A way to describe an experience using Situation, Task, Action, and Result. It is an option, not a mandatory script.
Invites you to describe a real experience, including one from study or a personal project.
Asks how you would handle a hypothetical situation. You do not need to pretend it has already happened.
An assignment completed independently within an agreed period. You can ask about scope, expected time, and evaluation criteria.
A discussion of subject knowledge and problem-solving. The format depends on the employer.
A discussion about the work environment and collaboration. It does not mean you must communicate like everyone else.
You can ask about the budget range and role scope before sharing your expectations.

entries.title: It is okay to clarify
entries.plain: You may ask for clarification before answering. This is not a measure of ability.

entries.title: Give yourself processing time
entries.plain: You may ask for a moment to think. Agree on the pause with the interviewer; you do not need to force an immediate answer.

entries.title: Choose how information is presented
entries.plain: You may ask to see a question in writing or have it split into parts. You do not need to disclose a diagnosis to describe useful support.
